reasons.ToleranceRelation: tolerance relations (: Writing tolerance relations (composite feature control frames) is out of scope for this stage (design: Out of scope); refused by name, left out of the round trip.
reasons.no part definitions: NIST FTC-08's -tg file is tessellated only: read_part_definitions finds no solid or shell with faces, so there is no part to write to (as for the reader).

patterns.key: specify-core: ISO 286 fit written as its deviations
patterns.reason: specify-core writes each ISO 286 class as the class's deviations only (TOLERANCE_VALUE, no LIMITS_AND_FITS), because OpenCascade writes the grade wrongly (specify-core writer.py; anti-requirement 'ISO 286 grade written wrongly'). haecceity writes the class the intent states as LIMITS_AND_FITS (§5.2.5); the deviations specify-core states are the class's (checked by the reader stage), so the meaning is the class, and haecceity's form is the practice's.

patterns.key: haecceity: ISO 286 fit written as LIMITS_AND_FITS
patterns.reason: The other side of the fit difference: the class written as PLUS_MINUS_TOLERANCE → LIMITS_AND_FITS(letter, 'hole'/'shaft', grade, '') (§5.2.5), read back as the same class.

patterns.key: haecceity: thread written as its THREAD entity
patterns.reason: specify-core writes threads as 'manufacturing requirement' text and a 'pmi-assist' attribute set because OpenCascade has no thread class (anti-requirement 'threads, knurls … appended as raw text'); haecceity writes the schema's THREAD with its shape_representation_with_parameters (thread WR1–WR16 checked). number_of_threads is written '1.' (one start): what the ratio counts is not settled (design: Status, open); the pitch is kept in the attribute set beside it.

patterns.key: specify-core: 'manufacturing requirement' text note (decision 5: not written)
patterns.reason: specify-core's 'manufacturing requirement' properties (surface texture, edge condition, general tolerance and thread/knurl text) are not a standard AP242 form; maintainer decision 5: not written. The general tolerance is written in its standard 'default tolerances' form and compares equal.

patterns.key: specify-core: thread as a 'pmi-assist' attribute set
patterns.reason: specify-core's user defined attribute set restating the thread (side, designation, pitch, class, hand, drill) because it cannot write THREAD; haecceity writes the THREAD itself and only what is not thread semantics (pitch, tapping drill, depths) as an attribute set.

patterns.key: haecceity: pitch, tapping drill and depths as an attribute set
patterns.reason: Tapping drill diameter and depth and full-thread depth are not thread semantics (design: Threads and knurls): a user defined attribute set on the thread's feature (UDA practice §5–7). The intent's pitch goes there too, since the schema's thread has no pitch item. 'through' is not written: a boolean_representation_item does not read back (reader gap reported).

patterns.key: specify-core: knurl as a 'pmi-assist' attribute set
patterns.reason: Independent evidence: crates/haecceity/tests/pmi_write.rs::intent_pmi handles the knurl intent in its catch-all arm, recording only a not-written message and omitting its stated pattern, pitch and diameter from PartPmi. The emitted STEP consequently has neither those manufacturing attributes nor their knurl feature binding. The AP242 turned_knurl WR2/WR9 parameter requirements justify refusing to invent a standard knurl, but do not justify losing the supplied information: it could remain explicit manufacturing attributes as thread pitch does in the same adapter. Cause: incomplete intent translation in the test adapter, not a failure of the writer to serialize a fully specified Knurl. Recorded without changing expectations or adding assumed DIN 82 parameters.

occt.key: datum_targets occt part 0 datum target A5
occt.reason: PMI practice v4.1 §6.6.1 Table 10 distinguishes circular curve (outline) from circle (enclosed area). XCAF 7.9.3 DatumTargetType has Point, Line, Rectangle, Circle and Area, with no circular-curve kind; this capture omits it. The writer retains the practice description and diameter; Rust reads it back exactly, and the unmodified rule engine reports only the authorized datum_target.WR5.

occt.detail: not read: Area(FeatureId(1))
occt.key: datum_targets occt part 0 datum target A6
occt.reason: PMI practice §6.6.2 Table 11 and NIST FTC-10 use a base datum_target for explicit area/curve geometry. OCCT 7.9.3 ReadDatums downcasts every target to PlacedDatumTargetFeature and skips base targets (STEPCAFControl_Reader.cxx 3032–3035); changing an area to placed would violate the non-exempt placed-target WR1. XCAF has no explicit curve target kind either. Rust preserves the standard geometry/target/datum; all four original FTC-10 areas pass clean-copy round trips. Raw schema/rule validation remains mandatory outside the reported target WR5.

OCCT 7.9.3 ReadDatums downcasts every target to PlacedDatumTargetFeature and skips base targets (STEPCAFControl_Reader.cxx 3032–3035); changing an area to placed would violate the non-exempt placed-target WR1. XCAF has no explicit curve target kind either. Rust preserves the standard geometry/target/datum; all four original FTC-10 areas pass clean-copy round trips. Raw schema/rule validation remains mandatory outside the reported target WR5.

occt.detail: XCAF exposes no general tolerance table or part decimal default
occt.key: datum_targets occt part 0 default table 0
occt.reason: PMI practice §4.1 Figure 3 decimal-only cell is written as COUNT_MEASURE(number of decimal places), with no invented range or tolerance. The raw rules still report cell WR3/WR4, individually listed on the new cell in practice_schema_conflicts per maintainer decision 2026-10-20. XCAF 7.9.3 exposes no default table or part decimal-place API. Rust reads both the named cell and bare part precision back exactly through Replace and resumed writes.

occt.detail: support instances [] vs [17]
occt.key: datum_targets_shared_support occt part 0 datum target A1
occt.reason: PMI practice §6.6.3 support feature, with a private composition endpoint (§5.1 Figure 31) when another tolerance controls the same feature. OCCT 7.9.3 ReadDatums only searches direct GISUs of the relating feature (STEPCAFControl_Reader.cxx 3055–3074), so it omits this support even though target type, number, placement and sizes read correctly. Using the ordinary aspect directly instead makes collectShapeAspect move/drop the other tolerance; the committed shared-support capture proves Position 0.05 stays on face #17. Rust preserves the support exactly and raw rules have only the authorized target WR5/cell WR3/WR4 conflicts.

Do not interpret these empty-PMI round trips as coverage of the newly written semantic forms.
